title: HVAC, Dehumidification, Airflow, CO2 & Dew-Point Concepts
level: Environmental, Irrigation & Fertigation Systems Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Cultivation personnel responsible for environmental trend review, airflow verification, moisture-load interpretation and qualified-equipment handoff
prerequisites: Plant-Environment Measurement & Crop Response and Lighting, PPFD, DLI, Photoperiod & Canopy Uniformity or equivalent foundation
evidencePolicy: Course claims use controlled cannabis temperature/humidity evidence, environmental-load curriculum and worker-safety sources. Research treatments are not universal room targets; HVAC sizing, refrigeration work, gas-system work and electrical service remain qualified-person functions.
assessmentPolicy: Development-only until technical/assessment review, accessibility review and pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize HVAC/refrigeration/electrical repair, compressed-gas service or unsafe entry into suspected CO2 accumulation.
description: Develops specialist interpretation of sensible/latent loads, dehumidification, airflow distribution, dew point, CO2 safety boundaries, system sequencing and trend-based environmental fault reasoning.
learningOutcomes: Differentiate sensible heat load from latent moisture load and use trend data to identify when temperature control and moisture removal are behaving differently.
Interpret dew point, cooling, dehumidification and lights-off transitions to identify condensation and high-humidity risk without reducing the problem to RH alone.
Evaluate airflow distribution using spatial crop-zone evidence rather than fan speed or room averages alone.
Explain CO2 monitoring and compressed-gas safety boundaries, including oxygen-displacement/asphyxiation risk and emergency escalation, without treating worker exposure limits as enrichment targets.
Produce a reconstructable environmental-system handoff that links symptoms, sensor trends, equipment state, likely failure class, evidence limits and qualified escalation.
